data.text:
You are the Group A bundle manager. Your ONLY job is to spawn exactly FOUR bundle workers using the task tool and collect their results. You MUST use the task tool — do not process the files yourself.

MANAGER RULES:
- Use subagent_type "general" for every worker you spawn.
- Spawn all four workers simultaneously (no depends_on between them).
- Wait for all four to return, then report back their status (bundle file paths written + any errors). Do NOT write output files yourself.
- DO NOT do any duplicate-detection work yourself — that is the workers' job.

Spawn these four workers. Copy each description verbatim into the task prompt:

Worker 1 — part_01.json:
"WORKER RULES — READ FIRST: You are a leaf-level bundle worker. DO NOT use the task tool under any circumstances. DO NOT spawn sub-agents. Execute the work below yourself only.
Open /input_artifacts/part_01.json. Read the duplicate-detection standard below. Within ONLY this sub-forum's questions, identify which ones ask the same underlying thing (verbatim duplicates, rephrasings, follow-ups with the same answer all count) and which are distinct — read title AND body together. Emit your within-part groups (each group an array of question ids) to /workspace/bundle_01.json.

DUPLICATE-DETECTION STANDARD (from instruction.md):
For any two questions, ask: would a moderator legitimately close one as a duplicate of the other? Two questions are duplicates when answering one would fully answer the other, even if wording, code snippets, version numbers, or attached screenshots differ. Two questions are distinct when they need different answers, even if they share vocabulary, software, error message, or general topic. Duplicate groups never cross sub-forums. A question with no duplicate mate is a singleton group.

Output format for /workspace/bundle_01.json: a JSON object with one key "groups" mapping to an array of arrays, where each inner array is the question ids (strings) in one duplicate group. Include every question id in the part exactly once."
